title: Coptic Calendar
intro: The Coptic calendar is the Alexandrian civil and religious chronology used by Egypt's Coptic Christian tradition and in agricultural dating.
epoch: Year 1 of the Anno Martyrum (A.M.) era begins in AD 284, associated with the reign of Diocletian. The New Year is called Nayrouz.
structure: Months 1–12 contain 30 days each. Month 13, Nasie, has five days ordinarily and six in the Alexandrian four-year leap cycle.
example: After day 30 of Mesori, Nasie completes the year; after its final day, the new year starts at Thout 1.
history: The calendar developed from the Alexandrian reform of the older Egyptian civil year and remains important in Coptic Orthodox life.
model: The provider uses the fixed Coptic/Alexandrian four-year leap cycle and the Coptic epoch; the underlying day coordinate is independent of the displayed era.
limits: This is the Coptic/Alexandrian arithmetic model, not ancient Egyptian regnal chronology. Month names vary by transliteration; Julian/Gregorian correspondences shift.
